mechanism_narrative: A higher unemployment rate (UNRATE) reflects deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce corporate profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Current UNRATE at 4.6% is above 5-year median of 4.0%
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of months when UNRATE exceeds its 5-year median, or the correlation between UNRATE and 5-day returns is not significantly negative (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 0.5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Current FEDFUNDS at 0.41% is below 0.5% threshold
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of months when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5%, or the average return in such months is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both labor market strength (PAYEMS) and housing demand (HOUST) signals a broad-based economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Current PAYEMS at 145128.0 and HOUST at 1323.0
failure_condition: The negative return signal fails to materialize in more than 50% of instances where both PAYEMS and HOUST decline from prior month, or the interaction term in a regression of 20-day returns on PAYEMS and HOUST is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), rising unemployment (UNRATE) has a stronger negative impact on S&P 500 returns due to stagflation concerns, leading to negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Current CPIAUCSL index of 242.348 implies ~3.0% annual inflation
failure_condition: In high inflation periods (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of months when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates weakening economic activity, reducing corporate earnings growth expectations and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Current INDPRO at 103.8589 is below 12-month moving average of 104.0
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of months when INDPRO declines from prior month, or the correlation between INDPRO and 60-day returns is not significantly negative (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When annualized inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it triggers a flight to safety and higher discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Current CPIAUCSL index of 242.348 implies ~3.0% annual inflation
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of months when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%, or the average return in such months is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (characterized by strong GDP growth and low unemployment), rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to policy tightening fears.
evidence_refs: fact:Current GDPC1 at 16712.5 indicates strong growth and UNRATE at 4.6% is low
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods (GDPC1 growth >2.0% and UNRATE <4.5%), the S&P 500 fails to produce negative returns when CPIAUCSL rises above 3.0% in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1300 thousand units, it signals a weakening housing market that reduces consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Current HOUST at 1323.0 is above 1300.0 threshold
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of months when HOUST falls below 1300.0, or the average return in such months is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).
